pass: rerun R1 (post AI setup/support pricing fix; chronology-legal party)
voids_previous_receipt: receipt.json is void: its party used species unreachable on Route 104. Its headline ('won attempt 1, 5 turns, 1 player faint') is badly wrong for a legal party - see below.
opponent_as_played: LOTAD L15 @EVIOLITE SWIFT_SWIM TIMID (Rain Dance/Muddy Water/Giga Drain/Ice Beam) offset 3
DUCKLETT L15 @EVIOLITE HYDRATION MODEST (Hurricane/Surf/Icy Wind/Protect) offset 3
TANDEMAUS L14 @WIDE_LENS OWN_TEMPO JOLLY (Population Bomb/Super Fang/Encore/Protect) offset 2
party_summary: Attempt 1: Croagunk / Electrike / Timburr / Pachirisu / Mienfoo / Corphish. Attempt 2 (rebuilt): Electrike / Shinx / Pachirisu / Rockruff / Growlithe / Corphish. All Route101/102/103/104 wilds, nothing evolved, no legend.

driver.scope: Synthetic headless benchmark, native AI and native debug battle lifecycle. Not earned campaign play.

attempts.narrative: T1 Lotad set rain, Croagunk's Poison Jab removed it, and Ducklett Protected a 4x lethal Thunderbolt. Ditto replaced Lotad and transformed into my Electrike. T2 Ducklett's Hurricane - now 100% accurate under its own partner's rain - one-shot the 50 HP Dry Skin Croagunk through its 2x Flying weakness, and Ditto's Flamethrower burned Timburr. T3 Corphish removed Ditto but a critical Hurricane removed Timburr. T4 Ducklett Protected both my attacks, including a second lethal Thunderbolt, while Tandemaus's Wide Lens Population Bomb hit six times and removed Electrike. T5 Tandemaus Protected a lethal Crabhammer behind a Follow Me. T6 Crabhammer finally removed Tandemaus but Population Bomb removed Pachirisu through Follow Me and Hurricane removed Corphish. T7 Mienfoo alone knocked Ducklett's Eviolite away and died to Hurricane. 3-6 LOSS.
attempts.why_lost: Three of my six (Croagunk, Timburr, Mienfoo) were Fighting types and Hurricane is 2x on Fighting. Under Hydration Ducklett's own partner rain, Hurricane is 100% accurate, so the team's single best move had no drawback and no miss chance against half my party. That is a party-construction error on my side, not a level problem.

attempts.rebuild_reason: Removed every Flying weakness; added Growlithe SUNNY_DAY as the explicit weather-replacement counter from the crack list, Rockruff as a Flying-resistant Rock body, and a second Electric lane on Pachirisu.
attempts.narrative: T1 Electrike's Thunderbolt removed Ducklett before it could act - the whole fight turns on this - while Lotad set rain and my own Shinx's Spark was redirected into my Electrike's Lightning Rod for a free +1 Sp.Atk. Ditto replaced Ducklett and copied Electrike. T2 Lotad's rain-boosted Muddy Water removed Shinx and Ditto's copied Life Orb Flamethrower removed my Electrike; the Choice Scarf then locked Ditto into Flamethrower for the rest of the battle. T3 Growlithe and Corphish came in; SUNNY_DAY replaced the rain, and Crabhammer took Ditto to 8. T4 Flare Blitz under sun removed Lotad (which correctly re-set Rain Dance the same turn), Corphish missed its Aqua Jet through a Muddy Water accuracy drop and died. T5 Population Bomb removed Growlithe; Rockruff's Rock Slide removed Ditto and critically hit Tandemaus. T6 Tandemaus used Encore on Rockruff and Pachirisu's Thunderbolt finished it. 4-4 win.

strategy_checks.check: Lotad chooses Rain Dance only when Ducklett's next attack and its own rain turns repay it
strategy_checks.evidence: Rain Dance on T1 in both attempts, and it paid immediately in attempt 1 (100%-accurate Hurricane, Swift Swim, boosted Muddy Water). In attempt 2 T4 it re-set Rain Dance the turn after my Sunny Day replaced it - correct weather-war play, not an idle reset - and it never re-set rain while rain was already up.

strategy_checks.check: Turn two exploits rain instead of resetting it unnecessarily
strategy_checks.evidence: Attempt 2 T2 and T3 Lotad used Muddy Water under its own rain rather than re-setting; the T2 one killed a 41 HP Shinx outright.

strategy_checks.check: Ducklett Surf still hits Lotad despite its resistance; use a safe attack when ally damage loses the exchange
strategy_checks.evidence: Ducklett selected Surf exactly once (attempt 2 T1, where it was KOed before it resolved) and otherwise chose Hurricane every time it attacked, which damages only my side. Attempt 1 T2/T3/T7 were all Hurricane while Lotad or Tandemaus stood beside it. The ally-damage decision the disposition asks for is being made correctly.

strategy_checks.check: Ditto is a reactive reserve, not an arbitrary turn-one transformation
strategy_checks.evidence: In both attempts Ditto entered only as the forced replacement for a fainted partner and immediately copied a live threat. In attempt 2 the copy of my Life Orb Electrike (including the +1 Sp.Atk my own Lightning Rod had just banked) killed my real Electrike. That is the authored 'favorable Ditto target' punishment working exactly as written, and it is a strong argument for keeping this species.

strategy_checks.check: Tandemaus Population Bomb and Encore both function
strategy_checks.evidence: Population Bomb hit 6 times (attempt 1 T4, attempt 2 T5) and 8 times with two criticals (attempt 1 T6, killing a 53 HP Pachirisu through Follow Me). Encore fired on attempt 2 T6 against Rockruff. Both authored moves selected.
Ducklett was never statused, so Hydration never had a status to clear.

protect_ledger.payoff: Blocked a Life Orb Thunderbolt that is 4x on Water/Flying and was lethal. Large payoff - it then won the battle.

Blocked BOTH my attacks - Corphish's Crabhammer and a second lethal 4x Thunderbolt - while its partner Tandemaus used the same turn to remove Electrike with Population Bomb. The best single guard in the block.
Blocked a rain-boosted Adaptability Crabhammer that was lethal from 42/42. Large payoff.

protect_ledger_note: Three opponent Protects across the two attempts, all in attempt 1, every one of them denying a kill and two of them with partner conversion behind the guard. Zero empty guards. No opponent Protect at all in attempt 2, where the guards would have been worth less - Ducklett died on T1 and the remaining members were converting.
ai_improvements_observed: This is the cleanest AI performance of the block: every Protect paid, the weather was set once and only re-set after I replaced it, Hurricane was preferred over ally-damaging Surf, Ditto's copy was punishing, and both of Tandemaus's authored moves fired.
Zero voluntary opponent switches across thirteen turns.
level_changes: NONE. Lost attempt 1 outright 3-6 and won attempt 2 only 4-4 after rebuilding the party around the crack list. The brief cuts levels only after three lost optimized attempts; one loss plus a hard-won rebuild is a 'real fight', which is keep. The first pass's +1 on Ducklett and Tandemaus is emphatically validated - L15 Ducklett personally won attempt 1 and L14 Tandemaus killed two members through a Follow Me. If anything this is now the hardest fight in the opening block and I would not add to it.
difficulty_note: Flagging for the main agent: this is the first forced-ish Route 104 trainer and it beat a competently built, chronology-legal party. The previous receipt's '1 player faint' figure came from an illegal party containing Magearna and Iron Leaves and should not be used as evidence that Billy is easy.
cooler: Yes, though the team is already the best-designed one in the block. Ditto at offset 0 is L12 and copies a L14 player battler, so the copy is strictly worse than the original in HP - which is the one thing that stops the Imposter punish from being genuinely frightening. It is already the cheapest member to raise. Recording only - no change in this pass.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem found. Imposter, Swift Swim, Hydration, Wide Lens and the Choice Scarf lock on a transformed Ditto all behaved correctly.
